lines.text: Meera has five hundred approved Hinglish replies, and a free Colab GPU. Can she really fine-tune a language model on that?
Not the usual way. Full fine-tuning updates billions of weights, and that needs far more memory.
LoRA takes a shortcut. Freeze every original weight. Then, beside each big matrix, add two thin ones, called an adapter.
Only the adapter is trained. That's usually well under one percent of the model.
At the start the adapter adds nothing, so the model behaves exactly like the original.
To fit a free T4, load the frozen model in four bits, and train the adapter on top. That's QLoRA.
Now training. Her examples go in, the loss falls, and the adapter slowly learns the brand's voice.
Watch the validation loss. If it climbs while training loss falls, the model is memorising.
Then the honest test: a question it never saw in training. Before, stiff English. After, friendly Hinglish.
What she publishes is tiny: megabytes, not gigabytes. Anyone can load the base model and put her adapter on top.
So remember: freeze the model, train a small adapter.
Next lesson: a FastAPI backend with streaming responses.
